grandparents_cupboard.reason: Bacon, onion, cauliflower, eggs, cheddar and thyme are all plain home staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: An ovenproof frying pan with a lid, a bowl and a grater are ordinary kit, and a frittata is within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: Eight eggs with a small cauliflower, six rashers and 75g cheddar makes a good lunch for four, and steaming the florets covered then baking at 200°C for 12 to 15 minutes will set it properly.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes of prep covers the chopping, grating and frying, and the covered steaming plus 12 to 15 minutes' baking fits the 20 cook minutes closely enough.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the thyme, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm cauliflower frittata suits a January lunch, and the cauliflower is the bulk of the filling.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: Eggs, bacon, cheese and a whole cauliflower make a filling, real-food lunch a family would happily eat again.
